items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1972-06-16
items.q: Yeah, I was playing with him.

ctx.x: I think there's some Strutter still in town. We could probably find his family. I mean, I think he must have some family here, because that name, I see it all over town, Strutter. Yeah, Strutter, it might. Yeah, we might catch up. Do you have something? Yeah, yeah, I wanted to ask you, what did David Jones play like? Was he any good?

Yeah, I was playing with him. Oh yeah? He played saxophone, he played everything. Mm-hmm. He played everything, boy. That's the only man I know could play a lot of French in one, boy. I'm in a place. I'm in a pool. I'm in a place. Mm-hmm. Professor Jones.

Well, did he always stay in New Orleans? What happened to him? He died. He went to California, he died. Mm-hmm, I see. He died in California. Yeah. Well, where did you first play with him? Huh? Where did you start in playing with Davy Jones? Professor Jones? Yeah, I did. In New Orleans? Yeah. What place? Uh, Historia.
